rounds.proof_sketch: num_features=64, update_block_size=256, update_blocks=1. Thread idx=64 executes in mutant (64>=65 is false). But running_mean/running_var have size 64, so idx=64 is out-of-bounds. Valid indices 0-63 are correctly updated. Output tensor is computed BEFORE update_running_stats_kernel (training) or uses only valid indices (inference).
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation allows thread 64 to execute and perform an out-of-bounds memory access to arrays of size 64. However, this out-of-bounds write doesn't corrupt the valid array elements at indices 0-63. In training mode, the output tensor is computed using batch_mean/batch_var before the running stats update kernel runs. In inference mode, the batchnorm kernel uses running_mean[feature_idx] where feature_idx is always in [0, num_features-1]. The out-of-bounds corruption affects memory outside the tensor, not the elements used for computation.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under current testing contract. The mutation causes out-of-bounds memory access but this doesn't affect the forward() output tensor. To detect this, one would need to inspect running_mean/running_var state after multiple forward passes, but the testing framework only compares output tensors.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing should include assertions on model state (running statistics) in addition to output tensors for stateful operations like BatchNorm. Consider adding memory sanitizer tests or bounds-checking kernels to detect out-of-bounds accesses that don't affect outputs.
